population.span: In this randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial, 172 adults scheduled for on‐pump CABG received colchicine or placebo.

endpoint.span: The primary outcome was incidence of postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF).

estimate.span: Of 163 analyzed patients (81 colchicine, 82 placebo), POAF incidence was significantly lower in the colchicine group (17.3% vs. 46.3%; RR 0.37, 95% CI 0.21–0.66;

treatment_strategy.span: received colchicine or placebo. The regimen included a preoperative loading dose (1 mg twice daily) followed by a weight‐based maintenance dose (0.5 mg daily if <70 kg; 1 mg daily if ≥70 kg) for 14 days.

gap_analysis_set.span: The primary analysis was conducted using a modified intention‐to‐treat approach.

gap_follow_up.span: The primary efficacy outcome was the incidence of any documented episode of POAF (defined as AF lasting ≥30 s) within the first 14 days after surgery.

gap_entry_age.span: Adult patients (aged 18–80 years) scheduled for elective on‐pump CABG were eligible.

analysis_set.absent_reason: Sources report 163 analyzed patients out of 172 enrolled adults but do not identify the analysis as ITT, mITT, per-protocol, or another defined analysis set.

typed_estimand.follow_up: The endpoint assessment duration is not stated. The 14-day treatment regimen does not establish follow-up or an in-hospital/index-admission assessment window.

extractor_mismatch_note: The served RR and confidence interval match the reported POAF result. However, the served intention-to-treat designation and in-hospital/index-admission timepoint are unsupported by the held sources.
